new_packages.label: בֵּן וְתַלְמִיד וּמַקִּיפִים
new_packages.reason: These concepts form an entirely independent and central conceptual domain in Torah 7 that is completely absent from the current dataset. The Torah's core argument in its first two-thirds (paragraphs aleph through yod) is built around the bechina relationship between ben (son) and talmid (student). The Rebbe explicitly states: 'ben ve-talmid kullu chad' — son and student are one. Yet he also distinguishes them: ben = dari ma'alah (upper-world perception, the 'mah' = unknowable transcendence); talmid = dari mata (lower-world perception, 'melo khal ha-aretz kevodo'). Makifim (surrounding/outer lights) are what the chakham receives when he empties himself to teach his students; keter is explicitly called bechina't makif; yovel is called bechina't klaliut ben ve-talmid; kohen is called bechina't klaliut ben ve-talmid; cherut = yovel. All these nodes are explicitly connected by bechina language in the source text, forming a coherent thematic family around the concept of intellectual transmission, spiritual legacy, and the structure of teacher-student relationship as the mechanism for receiving higher consciousness.

bechina_evidence.proof: וּבֶאֱמֶת בֵּן וְתַלְמִיד הוּא כֻּלּוֹ חַד
גַּם הַתַּלְמִיד הוּא בְּחִינַת בֵּן, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: כָּל הַמְלַמֵּד בֶּן חֲבֵרוֹ תּוֹרָה, כְּאִלּוּ עֲשָׂאוֹ
וְזֶה בְּחִינַת שֶׁפַע הַכֶּתֶר, כִּי כֶּתֶר הוּא בְּחִינַת מַקִּיף, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: כִּתְּרוּ אֶת בִּנְיָמִין

new_packages.justification_for_independence: This cluster is NOT part of Package 1 (emunah/tefilla) or any other existing package. The ben/talmid domain describes a separate thematic reality: the mechanism of intellectual-spiritual transmission between generations. While emunah/tefilla is about the individual's relationship with God through prayer, ben/talmid is about the tzaddik's relationship with his students and the structure of da'at (knowledge/consciousness) flowing through the generations. These are different answers to different questions: emunah answers 'how does one transcend nature?' while ben/talmid answers 'how does one's da'at outlive one's physical death?' The makifim/keter cluster then explains the spiritual reward (expansion of consciousness) that the chakham receives for this transmission — a concept entirely absent from the emunah/tefilla domain.

new_packages.label: מַלְכוּת וּפַרְנָסָה
new_packages.reason: The second major absent cluster in Torah 7 is the malkhut/parnasah domain. The Torah devotes paragraphs yod through yod-gimmel to explaining how malkhut (kingship) receives parnasah (sustenance) from the yadayim (hands = remezim/hints) in the sea of chokhmah. Livyatan is the bechina of malkhut; the yadayim are the bechina of remezim; the Temple is the bechina of klaliut ben ve-talmid AND the locus of parnasah (lechem ha-panim); Chanukah is the bechina of chanukat ha-bayit. These nodes all share the essential nature of the CHANNEL through which blessing flows from the upper worlds to the lower: from chokhmah's sea through yadayim to malkhut/Livyatan to parnasah for all creatures.

bechina_evidence.proof: לִוְיָתָן זֶה בְּחִינַת מַלְכוּת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: לִוְיָתָן נָחָשׁ בָּרִיחַ, לִוְיָתָן נָחָשׁ עֲקָלָּתוֹן, וּפֵרֵשׁ רַשִׁ"י: מַלְכוּת
אֵלּוּ הָרְמָזִים הֵם בְּחִינַת יָדַיִם, בְּחִינַת: נָטִיתִי יָדִי כַּנַּ"ל
כֵּן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ כָּלוּל מִבְּחִינוֹת בֵּן וְתַלְמִיד
מִזֶּה נַעֲשֶׂה בְּחִינַת חֲנֻכַּת הַבַּיִת, בְּחִינַת חֲנֻכָּה, הֶפֶךְ חֻרְבַּן הַבַּיִת

new_packages.justification_for_independence: This cluster is NOT an extension of Package 2 (etzah/nissu'in) or Package 4 (Yosef/brit/tzitzit). The malkhut/parnasah cluster describes a different thematic reality: the structural channel through which divine blessing flows downward into the material world. While Package 2 deals with the horizontal relationship (tzaddik-to-disciple counsel as zivug), Package B deals with the vertical channel (chokhmah's hands → malkhut → parnasah for all). The Livyatan/malkhut bechina is entirely independent — Livyatan is the cosmic symbol of malkhut's role as the great gatherer and distributor of divine sustenance. The Temple and Chanukah enter this cluster because the Torah explicitly ties chanukat ha-bayit to the restoration of parnasah and the illumination of aur ha-panim (the light of the face = makifim). Note that beit ha-Mikdash connects both proposed packages A and B, serving as a bridge node between the ben/talmid transmission axis and the malkhut/parnasah distribution axis — exactly as one would expect from the framework's cross-package traversal model.

observations:
Torah 7 of Likutay Moharan Tinyana presents a unique challenge for gap analysis: the existing dataset captures only the minor secondary conceptual domains of the Torah while leaving its two major primary domains entirely unrepresented.

The Torah's architecture has three major movements:

1. THE BEN/TALMID MOVEMENT (paragraphs aleph through yod, lines 1-80): The Rebbe teaches that the tzaddik must leave behind a son or student who carries his da'at forward. This entire movement is built on the bechina structure of ben ↔ talmid ↔ makifim ↔ keter ↔ dari ma'alah/dari mata. This is the Torah's primary philosophical claim and is entirely absent from the dataset.

2. THE MALKHUT/PARNASAH MOVEMENT (paragraphs yod through yod-gimmel, lines 65-105): The Torah then teaches how the tzaddik's transmission of wisdom (= yadayim/remezim in the sea of chokhmah) enables malkhut to receive parnasah. Malkhut = Livyatan, yadayim = remezim, Chanukah = chanukat ha-bayit. This is also absent from the dataset.

3. THE SECONDARY DOMAINS (scattered throughout): emunah/tefilla/nisim, Yosef/brit/tzitzit, etzah/nissu'in, shoruq/tipin/mochin — these ARE in the dataset.

The result is that the current dataset represents perhaps 30-40% of this Torah's bechina structure. The two proposed new packages (A: ben/talmid/makifim and B: malkhut/parnasah) together contain at least 15 nodes connected by at least 10-12 explicit bechina statements in the source text — far exceeding the threshold of 3+ concepts for a new package proposal.

Additionally, the closing note of the Torah (line 131) explicitly maps the Torah's concepts onto all ten sefirot: shefa ha-keter, chokhmah u-binah, yadayim (gam yirah), ben = chokhmah, shem ha-ben = tiferet, talmidim = netzach-hod, kol = yesod, malkhut. This Kabbalistic mapping confirms the structural independence of the ben/talmid cluster (chokhmah dimension) and the malkhut/parnasah cluster (malkhut dimension) as genuinely separate conceptual domains in the Torah's architecture.
